label: Intef II's column names Amun-Ra at Karnak
more: An eight-sided sandstone column inscribed by Intef II, found reused at Karnak, is the earliest firm evidence of a temple of Amun-Ra here. It suggests a small mud-brick shrine with a columned portico. Intef II reigned about 2112 to 2063 BC.

label: Akhenaten turns against Amun
more: In his fifth year, about 1348 BC, Akhenaten took his new name and attacked Amun. Amun's name was cut out of temples, wealth went to his new city Amarna, and the Amun temple was closed. He built the Gempaaten in east Karnak.

label: Tutankhamun restores the temples
more: After Akhenaten's death Tutankhamun reopened the temples. His Restoration Stela, found at Karnak in 1905, says they had fallen into ruin. It is dated year 4 by some scholars and year 1 by others, so about 1335 to 1332 BC.

label: Assyrians sack Thebes
more: Ashurbanipal's Assyrian army sacked Thebes and ended Kushite rule. Temples were reportedly plundered, but little damage has been found at the Amun-Ra temple itself. Shaw's chronology gives 664 BC; some books say 663.

label: Napoleon's scholars record Karnak
more: Napoleon's invasion of Egypt in 1798 brought scholars and artists. Denon reached Upper Egypt with the French army in winter 1798 to 1799, and his drawings of Karnak were among the first accurate European records. The Description de l'Égypte followed from 1809.

label: Mariette's Antiquities Service takes charge
more: The viceroy Said Pasha appointed the French Egyptologist Auguste Mariette to head a new antiquities service. It began Egypt's state control of digging and sites, including Karnak. It was renamed in 1971, 1994, 2011 and 2019.

label: Franco-Egyptian centre (CFEETK) founded
more: France's CNRS and Egypt's antiquities authority set up the Centre Franco-Égyptien d'Étude des Temples de Karnak to study, record and restore the temples. It publishes the Cahiers de Karnak.

label: Ancient Thebes made a World Heritage Site
more: UNESCO inscribed Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis (number 87) in 1979, under criteria (i), (iii) and (vi). It covers Karnak and Luxor on the east bank and the necropolis on the west.
